hints.content:
###Graphing the equations

The equations are both in *slope intercept form*: $y=\goldD{m}x+\purpleC{b}$. We can use the $y$-intercept and slope to identify points on each line.

The line given by the first equation $y=\goldD{-2}x+\purpleC{7}
$ has a $y$-intercept of $(0,\purpleC{7})$ and a slope of $\goldD{-2}$, so another point on that line is $(0+1,\purpleC{7}\goldD{-2})=(1,5).$ Now we have two points to graph this line.

In a similar manner, we will find that the line given by $y=\goldD{5}x\purpleC{-7}$ passes through $(0,\purpleC{-7})$ and $(0+1,\purpleC{-7}+\goldD{5})=(1,-2)$.

We can graph the lines using these points:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals negative two x plus seven is graphed with the points zero, seven and one, five plotted on the line. The equation y equals five x minus seven is graphed with the points zero, negative seven and one, negative two plotted on the line.

hints.content:
###Solving the system

When we graph the two lines, we can see that they intersect at $(2,3)$. Therefore, this is the solution of the system:

$\begin{align}
&x=2
\\\\
&y=3
\end{align}$

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The equation y equals negative two x plus seven is graphed with the points zero, seven and one, five plotted on the line. The equation y equals five x minus seven is graphed with the points zero, negative seven and one, negative two plotted on the line. The intersection of these two lines is plotted and labeled at two, three.
